I have been using Angular 2 for 3 months... Typescript awesomeness... Modular code... Template Directives... @angular/router is better than AngularJS routing... UI libraries for Angular... material2... are not complete yet and lack several useful components.

I use Angular 2 in production since November 19, 2015. Components are encapsulated and truly reusable... You don't need any 'bridges' anymore to use 3rd party JS libraries... Performance is great... Cool abilities like AOT-compilation, server-side rendering and tree-shaking.

The HTML template in Angular 2 is stored in a string... Editors can't do syntax coloring, auto-indenting, intellisense... Compilers can't find typos... You have to learn weird syntax such as ngFor whereas in React you just use a JavaScript for loop.
Angular's module syntax, while it makes sense, it's just easiest way to get version control merge conflicts.
Nodody mentioned angular universal here. I think it's a big win to prerender the SPA on the server. It's faster, more mobile friendly and pages can be indexed by search engines.

I worked on Angular last year... The worst however was when we started running into performance problems trying to render large tables... after about 8k-10k bindings, everything starts to crawl to a halt.

We built a pretty complex app with Angular (slimwiki.com) and have had nothing but great experiences. The main issues are no guidelines about the right/wrong way to do things, it needs to be more opinionated.

I've been using Angular on-and-off in professional settings since 2012. Angular is a framework obsessed with testability that treats usability as an afterthought... The middling quality and small availability of third-party Angular libraries is a problem.

The only issues I've run into are pages with large data bindings. I would love if the Angular team could recommend a solution other than 'don't do that.' That answer is simply unacceptable... their silence on this topic has been very frustrating.

I'm a big angularjs fan... selling points: Testing (Karma, Protractor, dependency injection) are fundamental when working with a team... Speed: no other framework makes front-end dev faster... Drawbacks: performance issues, probably too much hype.

I've been using Angular for a SaaS for 7 months... ~170 views, ~70 custom directives, ~100 controllers... I hit some situations where performance dropped a lot but if you take time to benchmark and test you can fix it.
As if we didn't have enough reason to move on from Angular. Now you need to learn Typescript to contribute or grok the source files?
So Angular has gone from being written in plain JS, to Dart, to Atscript, and now Typescript? Why so much jumping around? Isn't that creating a lot of technical debt issues?

Its the Angular 2 router that currently needs a lot more work. Currently things like passing data down to child routes, getting current route segments, checking active route etc are still not easily possible.

The foolish... mistake that Angular 2 made was using a template syntax that was almost but not quite completely unlike HTML... That is INVALID html and INVALID xml... you can't edit or process or generate or validate Angular templates with any of the millions of existing HTML and XML tools.

I prefer angular over react. It is opinionated (wasting time for decisions is bad); simpler to organize the code (it is MVC); (click)="onSelect()" is simpler than creating bind objects; I don't want web designers messing with my code.
